findings.claim: Section keys are not unique: the n-th copy of a slug gets `{base}-{n}` without checking that this key is free, and a heading can take a key that markers.py reserves, such as `written`.
findings.failure_scenario: A template with `## Notes`, `## Notes` and `## Notes 2` gives the second and third headings the same key `notes-2`. A heading titled `Written` gets the reserved key `written`. Because fill.assemble keeps one owned[key] dict, one section's text is lost and one model answer fills both sections. The body that `open` writes then has two `<!-- pr:begin notes-2 -->` markers, so every later `edit` is refused because markers.spans raises 'marker appears twice'.

f828dd2061.reason: Nothing reserves the marker key `written` for the header pair. In template.py lines 281-285, every heading's key is just `slug(title)`, so a heading `## Written` gets the key `written`. In fill.py, `plan_sections` (lines 242-248) marks a section that has text, or is empty, as `model`. `assemble` then sets `owned[s.key]` and wraps that section's content with `markers.wrap(s.key, content)` (lines 418-421). Lines 437-439 do the same for tail keys, and the extras in `src.extras` are not filtered either. Line 442 still writes the header pair `markers.written_line(written)` using the reserved key `WRITTEN = "written"` (markers.py lines 23 and 44-45). The body therefore holds two `<!-- pr:begin written -->` pairs. On the next `edit`, commands.py line 279 calls `markers.spans(current)`. That raises `marker `written` appears twice` (markers.py lines 70-71), and lines 280-281 turn it into a `Refused` error. So the PR body this skill created can never be edited by the skill. The scenario only happens when a template has a heading that slugs to `written`. That is an unusual template; neither the defaults nor the documented workflow produce one.

The trigger is a repo template with a heading whose slug is `written`. That is legal but unusual, and nothing in the repo's docs presents it as normal use, so the impact is correctness-only.

157cbadf24.reason: In template.parse (lines 281-285) a heading's key is its slug, or `{slug}-{n}` for the n-th copy, and nothing checks whether that key is already taken. Headings `Notes`, `Notes`, `Notes 2` get the keys notes, notes-2, notes-2. A heading `Written` gets the slug `written`, the key markers.py reserves for its own list (WRITTEN = "written"). Heading-only or text sections are planned as `model` (fill.py 242-248). fill.assemble stores the content in owned[s.key], so the later section overwrites the earlier one, and both sections read model_text.get(s.key). It still wraps each section in its own markers.wrap(s.key, ...), so the body holds two `pr:begin notes-2` markers, or two `written` pairs next to the managed header. The open gates (gates.run_open_gates) check headings, checkboxes, fill and word counts, but never call markers.spans, so `open` returns and writes the body. Any later parse goes through markers.spans, which raises 'marker ... appears twice'. That blocks edit/merge on this body. Impact is correctness-only: the failure needs a template with colliding headings (`X`, `X`, `X 2`) or a section titled `Written`, which is unusual for a repository PR template.
